title: Travelling to Vietnam – Questions & Tips
body:

[User #491575115 postsbillybalakalaiI just posted my opinion.Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
If you are someone who can't or doesn't want to think for themselves and loves to throw cash away - then tour packages are a great option.
They RARELY work out any cheaper than doing it yourself though, it all depends how much work you want to do.. If you want to plan the whole thing yourself, then of course it will be cheaper than paying someone else to organize everything..
[User #262031863 postssandyfreckleLife is short, it's also wide.Whirlpool Enthusiast] I have 'done' many trips to Vietnam…, it was just slightly difficult in 1989 but these days it is so easy. Tour groups can present themselves have some kind of exclusive 'inside info' because they hire local people or westerners with many trips under their belts…., that may be perfect for some people. Theses days it is so very easy to travel independently…, and most importantly you are not locked into a specific timetable etc.
My advice…, do lots of research on all the travel forums, work out what you want to do and where you want to go…, get yourself a 1 month visa and get out there. You will meet and interact with more locals and other travelers(if you need to)…, you'll have a much better time independently traveling around !

[User #54121522 postsRollinsI'm new here, please be nice] Hi We have recently returned from a two week trip to Vietnam. No tour and everything booked on line. Air Asia to Hanoi, Vietnam airlines to Hue, Train Hue to Hoi Na (Da Nang station) Vietnam airlines to Ho Chi Min and AirAsia out. Never tour as my wife is not an early morning person and dread getting her up early. All hotels booked directly or using Booking.com who's website is great. Research was mainly through Trip Advisor and Whirlpool. Love the flexibility of doing what we want. Of course you can do it yourselves – I am 68 years old and my wife is 64. Enjoy Vietnam Greg Lander
[User #534501428 postsDirtTurtleForum Regular] C is for cake writes...
Has anyone done a tour of Vietnam by themselves rather than going through a tour package? If so how did it work out? Or is a tour package the best option?
I'm heading back to Vietnam for my third time, and in 3 years. Absolutely love the place. First was semi-organized by a travel agent but have since been organizing my own travel.
I'm not an experienced traveler like Sandyfreckle but from an amateurs perspective found it so easy thanks to modern technology (only been to 3 main travelers cities etc and not out in the sticks).
Like Sandy eluded to look online, so much information its not funny. Also found it handy to have a decent phone GPS with data so that you can quick search for locations, restaurants etc on the fly. Day tours are very easy to book if you want, although I think the demand of Ha Long Bay would mean you would need to book it well in advance.
Clwy also stated about the people, communication is easy enough without English for basics. In Ho Chi Minh I found the people more open to talking English or being approachable. Hanoi the people seemed a lot more reserved but so happy to help it almost every occasion. I recall having a Google Translator conversation in a Viettel store with two young guys trying to find a store I needed. They were quiet and more than happy to sit their on the PC having a go with nothing to do with their store.
Very surprised about the dollar value for the accommodation, I've booked a couple of places thinking the reviews were too good to be true for the price but were fantastic.
Vietnam is an open slather for booking yourself.

[User #37828817772 postswatto23Will do anything to travelWhirlpool Forums Addict] DirtTurtle writes...
Very surprised about the dollar value for the accommodation, I've booked a couple of places thinking the reviews were too good to be true for the price but were fantastic.
Yep I also found Cambodia was the same. I've yet to go to Laos. But i got a double room for myself in Siem Reap for $9 with A/C and free wifi. I could have had a fan only for $6.
When I went to Vietnam we booked as we went as internet booking wasn't as common. Still I remember forking out for the luxurious $10 rooms over $5 rooms on many occasions. Probably not that cheap now, but its still a cheap place to travel.
Vietnam is an open slather for booking yourself.
Another story was a tour I booked on Halong Bay. Cost me $12 for an overnight trip. Accomodation was average, but it was $12. However on the boat one couple booked via a travel agent in NZ and paid $200, another booked the trip from HCMC and paid $50.
